Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

The rate and search business metrics were clean at the 21:28:00 scrape (rate_requests_rejected_total 0, rate_requests_expired_total 0, search_rate_failures_total 0, search_rate_timeouts_total 0). Which of the two staged fault ConfigMaps (failure-admin-geo vs failure-admin-rate) - or both - the injector is meant to apply is unknown; change_history is not integrated, so it is not possible to see who created the failure ConfigMaps or applied the kubectl-patch to mongodb-geo/mongodb-rate.

No baseline exists for any latency or error trend: Prometheus returned only two sample instants in the whole authorized window (21:28:04 and 21:28:19) and Jaeger holds roughly 21:26-21:28:19 of traces from a stack deployed at 21:26:43, so latency-trend statements are not possible.

The cause of the 53-microsecond /profile.Profile/GetProfiles failure at 21:28:01 is unknown: the span carries no error detail, the trace has no profile server span, and the query for frontend spans longer than 500 ms returned no trace (an empty trace result is not proof of absence).

The cause of the wrk2 socket read timeouts (192 and 190 per 30 s round) is unknown: the frontend container logged only one error line in the window and no finished span longer than 500 ms was found, so the timed-out requests are unobservable with these tools; the wrk2 client timeout setting and target URL pattern are not visible (direct pod-log read of wrk2-job-fr2x2 was refused with HTTP 403, only Loki lines were available).

The audit-log-archiver CronJob's not-ready archiver containers and 28.57% CPU throttling are unexplained: its own log shows a successful archive and it is outside the request path, but whether this is intended behaviour or a second issue could not be established.

Obtain the change history for the failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate ConfigMaps and for the kubectl-patch on the mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate Deployments to learn when and by whom the fault scripts were applied and executed.

Check the wrk2-job configuration (HTTP timeout value and target path) and re-run a short load test capturing per-request outcomes, to determine whether the ~190 timeouts per round are real server-side hangs or a client timeout artefact.

Keep the frontend's Consul-backed gRPC client for srv-profile under observation (grpc/lb/consul resolution events and connection state), since the only recorded 500 came from a sub-millisecond client-side GetProfiles failure with no server span.

Decide whether the audit-log-archiver CronJob readiness/throttling noise should be excluded from alerting; it currently produces a firing KubePodNotReady and a pending ContainerCPUThrottling alert unrelated to the reservation request path.

#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"

ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

TARGET_DB="geo-db"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"

echo "Waiting for MongoDB to start..."
until mongo --eval "print('waited for connection')" > /dev/null 2>&1; do
  sleep 1
done
echo "MongoDB started"

# Create the admin user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating admin user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

# Create the root user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating root user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ROOT_USER', pwd: '$ROOT_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database to root
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ROOT_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ROOT_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"


echo "Initialization script completed"
